for my fiancée

som& oma

A long-distance love story built with prayer, patience, late calls, laughter, little gifts, and the quiet mercy of God.

Some love stories are remembered through photographs. Ours was also carried through glowing screens, ordinary calls, private laughter, prayer, and the simple decision to keep showing up for one another.

Loving you was my beginning to my journey to God.

chapter one

Before you, I was already tired.

When I first noticed you, I was not in a place of casual excitement anymore. I had been through enough emotional confusion to know that games and heartbreak could waste years. I had been broken before, and if I am being honest, I had also broken hearts too. One relationship after another had taught me that human effort alone could not produce the kind of love I wanted to build a life on.

The last serious experience I had left me with one strong lesson: if I was going to get this part of my life right, I needed to wait for God. Around that season, I was already praying intensely for over a hundred days about something completely different. Unknown to me, while I was praying, God was already arranging the person who would become part of my restraint, my growth, and my future journey — especially with everything ahead of me in the UK.

I did not know it was you yet. I only knew I was tired of shallow love.

chapter two

Then came a follow back.

We officially started talking on Instagram, not knowing we were already friends on Facebook. The first message was simple: “follow back.” You were online. You replied. There was energy immediately. It felt light, effortless, alive.

Still, I did not rush. It had taken me almost three months — from October to the beginning of December — to even give myself permission to follow you properly. You kept appearing on my Instagram in a way that felt louder than coincidence. But even then I was hesitant. Part of me wanted to walk away before feelings had the chance to become serious.

Funny enough, one of the first things I remember is you asking me to help choose a dress for an event. You did not know how much that simple moment stayed with me. Later, I boldly asked for a full photo of you in leggings or tight jeans. You dribbled me very well. I did not know there was a whole story behind that. But you sent another full photo in an Ankara outfit, and even the sight of your foot in that picture felt so beautiful to me that I knew something dangerous was happening in my heart. I remember thinking, if I continue like this, I will fall in love hopelessly.

chapter three

The word in my spirit was: wait.

At first, I made assumptions about you. I wondered whether your heart really leaned toward the things of God. I saw hints that made me uncertain, and because I had been wounded before, my instinct was to protect myself early. But while my mind was trying to run, my inward witness kept saying something very different: wait.

That word saved the story. Instead of pushing you, controlling you, or trying to edit you into the version of a woman I thought I wanted, I stayed patient. I did not pressure you about the events you attended. I did not try to force outward change. I simply waited and listened.

Then I made the proposal that mattered most: let us read the Bible together; let us read godly books together. You accepted. That yes was the real beginning. What started as a conversation became spiritual companionship. What looked casual began to turn into something sacred.

chapter four

I watched grace happen in front of me.

One of the beautiful gifts of our story is that I did not only hear you talk about God — I watched God work in you. I saw you begin to speak in tongues right there in front of me. I wish I had recorded that moment. It was beautiful. I also watched you read more confidently out loud. Because of your shyness, bold public reading did not come naturally at first, yet I watched you grow into it.

I saw a woman becoming more beautiful than she already was. Not just outwardly, but spiritually. I saw you discerning. I saw you learning to hear from your spirit. I saw softness and strength forming side by side.

That is one of the reasons you became so precious to me. You were not just attractive to me. You were becoming a witness of grace to me.

chapter five

The argument that changed our language.

We were not a perfect story with no hard moments. We had issues. There were dark times. There were moments when we almost gave up. I do not want to build a false love story by removing all the painful memories, because the truth is that those difficult places also became part of what made us stronger.

One of the most important conversations happened around February, close to Valentine’s Day last year. You kept saying you had prayed for a man like me. In my heart I felt the same about you, but I still resisted giving our relationship the ordinary language of modern romance. I believed we should only be friends, then court, then marry. To me, “dating” felt unnecessary or even wrong. I said human love was too impure and that what we should really strive for was God-kind love expressed fully in marriage.

But you argued with wisdom. You told me that people first experience human love before they learn how to grow into God-kind love inside marriage. That argument stayed with me. It moved something. You won me there.

You helped me understand that love can begin in humanity and still be trained toward holiness.
chapter six

The night I said I love you.

On the night of Valentine’s Day, I finally told you I loved you. After all the arguments in my head, after trying to keep you in the category of “friend,” after pretending that my heart was not already involved, I said the words.

And then you answered: “thank you.”

Then you left the call. For three days I could not reach you properly. I cried. I felt exposed, confused, almost betrayed by my own honesty. In my mind, I even told myself that I was not supposed to love you that way — only as a friend. But the truth had already come out.

On the third night, I spoke to you honestly about how much I was struggling. Then you told me you loved me too, but you did not know what had happened to you. By then, something had shifted for good. The woman I said “I love you” to became the woman I now call my fiancée.

chapter seven

Long distance taught us another kind of closeness.

We have only done long distance, but distance did not empty the relationship. It only changed the way love had to travel. We learned to live through calls, screen records, ordinary check-ins, gifts on special days, prayers at night, and the quiet discipline of staying emotionally present.

You became my shawarma babe. My baby. My love. And even though the miles were real, I always wanted to close the gap in every way I could, especially on the days you needed to feel celebrated.

That is why these screen-recorded moments matter to me. They are not polished, and that is exactly why they are beautiful. They hold the actual atmosphere of us.

chapter eight

What our struggle taught me.

1
Our struggles made us stronger.
The beautiful parts of our story shine more because they survived the difficult parts.
2
Your weakness and mine taught us humility.
Instead of pretending to be perfect, we kept learning how much we needed grace.
3
The Holy Spirit truly carried us.
Through dark moments, confusion, and the times we nearly let go, He kept us from losing the story completely.
4
Love must be guarded, not assumed.
I pray God will keep us from cheating, dishonesty, disloyalty, pride, and every quiet thing that weakens union.
5
What I ask God for now is increase.
May He keep teaching me how to love you well, and may my love for you keep increasing.
chapter nine

What comes next.

So much of our love has happened through separate screens, but our story is not ending there. Very soon, this distance that shaped us will give way to something more solid. By the end of January next year, I will not be meeting you merely as the man on the other side of the phone. I will be meeting you as your husband.

We will still take the beautiful couple photographs when that time comes. But before those future photos arrive, I wanted to honor this chapter too — the chapter where we learned to stay, learned to pray, learned to forgive, learned to laugh, learned to argue and still come back, learned to hear God, and learned that love can grow even when two people are not yet in the same room.

Hillsongs has quietly lived in the background of parts of this journey. Prayer has lived in the center of it. And you, my baby, my Oma, my Nkem, have lived in the heart of it.

There are easier stories, and there are truer stories. Ours is true.
for my fiancée

Oma, my love.

Thank you for becoming part of my journey to God, and for letting me become part of yours. Thank you for staying through the parts that were tender, confusing, joyful, and difficult. Thank you for receiving my honesty and for teaching me, sometimes gently and sometimes firmly, what love could still become.

I do not just want a beautiful love story with you. I want a faithful one. One that keeps growing cleaner, deeper, softer, and stronger. One that can survive distance and still know how to arrive.

And if this page has one simple message underneath all the others, it is this: I love you, baby — and I am grateful that God let our paths meet, wait, grow, and stay.

Som.
